intro: OPC UA (Open Platform Communications Unified Architecture) is a client–server protocol used across industrial software. A server offers an address space: nodes (folders, objects, variables …) with names, types and values, linked by references. A client, the program that asks, first opens a secure channel, which sets how messages are protected. Then it opens a session, which ties its work to a user. Now it can browse, read, write or subscribe to changes.
plain: This protocol lets a control program look inside a machine's controller and find any value by name, like browsing the folders on a computer. The program first agrees with the controller on how to protect their talk, and says who it is. Then it can read a value, change a setting, or ask to be told each time a value changes.

hello.title: Say hello
hello.text: The client opens a network connection (TCP) to port 4840. It says Hello: the largest pieces of data it can take (its buffer sizes), and the endpoint it wants, the server address it is calling. The server acknowledges with its own limits.

channel.title: Open a secure channel
channel.text: OpenSecureChannel sets how messages are protected. Signing proves who sent a message and that nobody changed it; encryption hides what it says. Here the security policy is None: no signing, no encryption. The server gives the channel the number 5.

session.title: Start a session
session.text: CreateSession and ActivateSession tie a user to the channel. The client gets an authentication token, a secret ID like a visitor's badge. It puts the token in every later request.

browse.title: Browse the server
browse.text: The client looks through the address space, starting at the Objects folder, like opening folders on a disk. It finds the object PV1, an inverter, and its variable TotW: the total active power, the power the inverter delivers.

read.title: Read a value
read.text: Read asks for attribute 13, the Value, of the node ns=2;s=PV1.TotW. This NodeId, the node's address, means: in namespace 2 (the controller maker's own set of names), the string PV1.TotW. The answer is a Float, a decimal number in 4 bytes: 4820.0. It comes with two timestamps: when the value was measured, and when the server read it.

subscribe.title: Subscribe to changes
subscribe.text: The client asks the server to watch TotW. It keeps a Publish request waiting at the server, like an open question. When the value changes, the server answers it.

frames.hel: Hello: these are my buffer sizes
frames.opn-req: Open a secure channel, with no security
frames.create-req: Please create a session for me
frames.create-resp: Here are your session and its token
frames.browse-req: What is in the Objects folder?
frames.read-req: What is the value of PV1.TotW?
frames.monitor: Watch TotW and tell me when it changes

notes.create-req: A MSG with a CreateSessionRequest: the client's name and certificate, a nonce (a random number used once), and how long the session may stay idle.
notes.create-resp: The server returns a session ID, the authentication token, its endpoints and its certificate. The token is secret: whoever has it can use the session.
notes.activate-req: ActivateSession with an anonymous identity token. A real user sends a name and a password encrypted for the server, or a user certificate.
notes.activate-resp: The session is active. If it stays idle longer than the time agreed in CreateSession, the server closes it.
notes.browse-req: Browse from node i=85, the Objects folder, following its hierarchical references: the links from a folder to what is inside it.
notes.browse-resp: A list of references, each with a NodeId, a browse name and a node class. ns=2;s=PV1 is an object; ns=2;s=PV1.TotW is a variable inside it.
notes.monitor: Two requests, each with its response. CreateSubscription sets a publishing interval of 1000 ms: once a second, the server sends what has changed, if anything has. CreateMonitoredItems makes the server sample TotW every 500 ms. Then the client sends Publish requests ahead of time.
notes.publish: A PublishResponse with a data change notification: the client's handle for TotW (the number it chose for this item), its new value and timestamps. The client acknowledges it in its next Publish request.

msg.name: MSG
msg.note: Message type: a service message on an open channel.

final.name: F
final.note: The final chunk (piece) of the message. Here it is also the only one.

size-56.name: Message size
size-56.note: 0x38 = 56 bytes, the whole message. Every number in OPC UA is sent low byte first.

uacp-version.name: Protocol version
uacp-version.note: 0: the version of this connection protocol (UA TCP).

rx-buffer.name: Receive buffer
rx-buffer.note: 65536 bytes: the largest chunk the client can take.

tx-buffer.name: Send buffer
tx-buffer.note: 65536 bytes: the largest chunk the client will send.

max-message.name: Max message size
max-message.note: 16777216 bytes (16 MB): the largest response the client accepts, all its chunks together.

max-chunks.name: Max chunk count
max-chunks.note: 0: a response may have any number of chunks.

url.name: Endpoint URL
url.note: A length of 24, then "opc.tcp://10.0.0.40:4840": the endpoint the client wants.

rx-buffer-server.name: Receive buffer
rx-buffer-server.note: 65536 bytes. The server may lower the client's sizes, never raise them.

tx-buffer-server.name: Send buffer
tx-buffer-server.note: 65536 bytes: no larger than the client's receive buffer.

max-message-server.name: Max message size
max-message-server.note: 16 MB: the largest request the server accepts.

max-chunks-server.name: Max chunk count
max-chunks-server.note: 0x100 = 256: a request may have at most 256 chunks.

channel-0.name: Secure channel ID
channel-0.note: 0: there is no channel yet. The server picks the number.

policy.name: Security policy
policy.note: A length of 47, then http://opcfoundation.org/UA/SecurityPolicy#None: no signing, no encryption.

no-cert.name: Sender certificate
no-cert.note: Length -1: none. With a real policy, the sender's X.509 certificate goes here.

no-thumb.name: Receiver thumbprint
no-thumb.note: Length -1: none. With a real policy: the thumbprint (a short hash) of the receiver's certificate.

seq-1.name: Sequence number
seq-1.note: 1: the client counts every chunk it sends on this channel.

req-1.name: Request ID
req-1.note: 1. The response carries the same ID.

type-446.name: Type
type-446.note: A NodeId in 4 bytes: namespace 0, number 446 (0x01BE): OpenSecureChannelRequest.

no-token.name: Authentication token
no-token.note: A null NodeId: there is no session yet.

t-opn.name: Timestamp
t-opn.note: 10:41:05.120 UTC: a 64-bit count of 100 ns steps since 1601.

handle-1.name: Request handle
handle-1.note: 1: a number the client uses to match the answer.

diag-audit.name: Diagnostics · audit
diag-audit.note: Return diagnostics 0 (none wanted), then an audit entry ID of length -1 (none).

timeout.name: Timeout hint
timeout.note: 0x2710 = 10000 ms: how long the client will wait.

no-header.name: Additional header
no-header.note: An empty extension object: no extra header fields.

ua-version.name: Protocol version
ua-version.note: 0: the protocol version of the sender.

issue.name: Request type
issue.note: 0: issue a new security token. 1 would renew one.

client-nonce.name: Client nonce
client-nonce.note: Length 0: with the policy None no keys are made, so no random number is needed.

lifetime.name: Requested lifetime
lifetime.note: 0x0036EE80 = 3600000 ms: the token should last one hour. The client will renew it before then.

channel-5.name: Secure channel ID
channel-5.note: 5: the number the server gave this channel.

seq-1-server.name: Sequence number
seq-1-server.note: 1: the server counts its own chunks.

handle-1-resp.name: Request handle
handle-1-resp.note: 1, the same as in the request.

no-diag.name: Diagnostics
no-diag.note: An empty diagnostic info (mask 0), then an empty string table.

token-id.name: Token ID
token-id.note: 1: every later message names this token.

created.name: Created at
created.note: When the server made the token.

revised.name: Revised lifetime
revised.note: 3600000 ms: the server accepts one hour.

seq-5.name: Sequence number
seq-5.note: 5: the client's fifth chunk on this channel.

auth-token.name: Authentication token
auth-token.note: A GUID NodeId (0x04) in namespace 1, given by CreateSession. It ties the request to the session.

max-age.name: Max age
max-age.note: A double, 0.0 ms: read the current value, not a cached one.

both.name: Timestamps to return
both.note: 2: both, the source's and the server's.

node.name: NodeId
node.note: 0x03: a string NodeId. Namespace 2, then a length of 8 and "PV1.TotW".

attr-13.name: Attribute ID
attr-13.note: 13: Value. Other attributes give the node's name, its data type, its access level …

no-range.name: Index range
no-range.note: Null: the whole value, not a part of an array.

no-encoding.name: Data encoding
no-encoding.note: A null name in namespace 0: the default encoding.

seq-5-server.name: Sequence number
seq-5-server.note: 5: the server's fifth chunk on this channel.

results-1.name: Results
results-1.note: An array of one result, for the one node asked for.

mask.name: DataValue mask
mask.note: 0x0D: a value, a source timestamp and a server timestamp follow. No status code means Good.

float.name: Variant type
float.note: 0x0A = 10: Float, a decimal number in 4 bytes.

value.name: Value
value.note: 4820.0, low byte first. The unit, kW, is a property of the node (EngineeringUnits).

source-time.name: Source timestamp
source-time.note: 10:41:06.000 UTC: when the controller measured the value.

server-time.name: Server timestamp
server-time.note: 10:41:06.302 UTC: when the server read it.

a-ns.name: Namespace index
a-ns.note: 2: a position in the server's namespace array. 0 is the OPC UA standard's own; 2 here is the controller maker's.

a-kind.name: Identifier type
a-kind.note: s: a string. i is a number, g a GUID, b a byte string.

a-id.name: Identifier
a-id.note: PV1.TotW: the name the server gave the node.

facts.standard: IEC 62541 (OPC UA). Part 6: binary encoding and UA TCP
facts.between: Client (SCADA, HMI, historian) → server (plant controller, PLC, turbine)
facts.security: Secure channel with X.509 certificates: None, Sign or SignAndEncrypt
facts.model: Address space: nodes in namespaces, linked by references

tips: This lesson uses the security mode None so that the bytes can be read. On a site, use SignAndEncrypt with a current policy such as Basic256Sha256. Sign alone stops anyone from changing the messages, but anyone on the network can still read the values.

Both sides must trust each other's certificate. Many first connections fail because the server has put the client's certificate in its rejected list. An administrator must move it to the trusted list.
Namespace indexes can change when the server restarts or is updated. Store the namespace URI with each NodeId, and look up its index after you connect.
Do not poll, that is, send Read many times a second. A subscription with a sampling and a publishing interval costs the server far less.

anatomy.nodeid: A NodeId: where a value lives in the address space

playground.encoder: OPC UA sends numbers low byte first (DCBA), unlike MMS. 4820.0 travels as 00 A0 96 45.
